claims.statement: URE describes a guarantee of origin as the document certifying to an end customer that a specified amount of energy was produced from renewable sources; it is issued electronically and recorded in the guarantee registry.
URE states that a guarantee is valid for 12 months after the relevant production period and can be sold to another holder and retired through the registry; it does not itself create property rights.
Hypothesis: administrative reliability and pooled volume can win recurring mandates from subscale generators; unclaimed volume and attainable commission are not yet evidenced.

contrary_evidence: URE explicitly says guarantees of origin do not carry property rights, so the opportunity depends on agency contracts and service quality rather than owning an intrinsically appreciating asset.
The 12-month validity window creates operational urgency but also expiry risk and weak bargaining power for fragmented sellers.

economics.acquisition_route: Start with ten eligible generators introduced through installers, verify forgone volumes and process burden, then match only evidenced inventory to two procurement partners.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Unvalidated path: 1.2m MWh of annual mandated volume at PLN 3 average commission plus PLN 0.9m reporting revenue yields about PLN 4.5m revenue; at 25% operating profit and a 6x value, a 75% founder stake is about PLN 5.1m. Reaching that scale in 7-10 years requires durable producer mandates and repeat buyers, not speculative certificate inventory.
economics.founder_time: 8-12 hours per week during a pilot, concentrated around onboarding, reconciliation and exceptions; registry execution and regulated energy advice stay with qualified counterparties.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Unvalidated estimate: 60-75% after registry, energy-adviser and transaction support, provided administration is automated and the business does not warehouse price risk.
economics.payback: Unvalidated target: 9-15 months at roughly 100,000-200,000 MWh of annual mandated volume, subject to realized commission and fixed administration fees.
economics.pricing: Unvalidated hypothesis: PLN 2-6 per transferred MWh plus PLN 3,000-15,000 annual administration for complex generators or buyer portfolios; actual spreads must be tested and transparently disclosed.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Generation recurs every year, so correctly timed applications and reliable settlement can renew without reacquiring the producer; buyer renewals depend on reporting quality and competitive price.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: contracted recurring production creates forward visibility, while a diversified portfolio and clean operational record make the agency more useful to repeat buyers
fingerprint.customer: small renewable generators that under-monetize guarantees of origin and mid-market electricity buyers seeking documented renewable origin
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: renewable installers, accountants, producer associations and electricity advisers introduce generators; buyer demand is acquired through sustainability and energy-procurement partners
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: calendar administration, volume aggregation, matched procurement and retirement evidence sold as agency brokerage plus an optional annual portfolio-reporting fee
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: generator and/or buyer pays a disclosed PLN-per-MWh commission only when a guarantee is transferred or retired according to mandate
fingerprint.problem_trigger: a generator misses application or expiry windows, or a buyer needs auditable origin evidence in a volume and profile too small for a large bespoke procurement desk

founder_fit: Uses renewable-sector access, quantitative reconciliation and workflow automation.
Can be validated without financing power assets or taking commodity price exposure.
Recurring production supports a compounding contracted portfolio.
Partner and process distribution can limit high-energy founder selling.
risks: Guarantee prices and commissions may be too thin for small portfolios.
Registry or brokerage functions may require memberships, contracts or licensed intermediaries.
Large energy suppliers may bundle the service and compress margins.
Double counting or misleading environmental claims would create legal and reputational exposure.

structure.control_point: multi-year exclusive marketing mandates over recurring eligible generation volumes, paired with reliable application and expiry operations
structure.critical_dependency: enough generators must be eligible, willing to mandate recurring volumes, and able to execute registry transfers to buyers that value the resulting portfolio

thesis: Secure recurring, exclusive marketing mandates from overlooked Polish renewable generators and aggregate their future guarantees of origin into buyer-ready portfolios by technology, region and production period. Handle application calendars, registry instructions and retirement evidence through compliant partners, then earn a disclosed commission or spread only on transferred volumes. This is an agency around recurring production rights, not a claim that guarantees themselves confer energy ownership or guaranteed price appreciation.
title: Recurring Guarantee-of-Origin Portfolio Agency
uncertainties: How much eligible generation is currently unmanaged or poorly monetized among target producers?
What mandate duration and minimum volume will producers accept?
Which buyer segments pay for technology, geography or production-period specificity?
Can cross-border AIB access be obtained economically through a partner if needed?
